reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) discusses EDS characterization of diffusion in Ni/Fe/Cr systems, non-uniform diffusion due to temperature gradients, and general ATF cladding strategies mentioning CrN as a ceramic coating, but none provides specific prior data on nitrogen ion implantation into Cr coatings, the formation of a near-interface CrN barrier, its efficacy as a diffusion barrier for Cr–Zr, or its performance under the specified conditions. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nitrogen ion implantation can produce a uniform, near-interface CrN barrier in a Cr coating on Zr-alloy.
CrN precipitates act as a diffusion barrier that hinders atomic mobility of Cr and Zr.
The CrN barrier will significantly reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion at ~1200 °C in steam.
The CrN barrier will retain protective properties under ~350 °C subcritical water.
